title: Reframe PROP-115 — operator REJECTS throttle direction, COMMISSIONS a deeper-value reframe. We are willing to spend the money during the quiet period. Use this time to build forward-value reserves before dome activity returns and pipeline competition spikes.
context:
Tinker authored PROP-115 (2026-06-28T02:49Z) proposing to throttle itself from daily to every-other-day during the quiet period (~$6.40/day saved, ~50% of tinker spend). The reasoning is sound — tinker IS now the #1 per-run cost agent at $12.77/run, and the 2026-06-23 quiet-period sweep did skip tinker.

The operator is REJECTING Recommendation A (throttle) for a strategic reason that's NOT visible in PROP-115's cost framing:

QUIET PERIOD = ZERO MARGINAL CONFLICT WINDOW. During day 72 of dome drought with the entire upstream chain at 1/day cadence, tinker doing deep audit work doesn't conflict with anything. Once the dome breaks drought (likely within 30-60d, with eclipse T-45 and PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 closing in 2d), the pipeline will compete for tinker's attention: new analyst Mode 0 work, curmudgeon discovery on fresh content, decider intake backlogs, integrity findings on broken assertions — all things tinker would have to handle on top of routine ops. THAT is when tinker capacity is precious.

Operator framing: the right time to spend on deep tinker analysis is RIGHT NOW, not after dome returns. The right time to throttle tinker is AFTER we've harvested all the deep-value work, IF cost pressure justifies. We're nowhere near cost pressure — quota usage is on pace for ~38% weekly, well below quota ceiling.

So: instead of asking 'how do we make tinker cheaper', the question is 'how do we make tinker MORE VALUABLE during the cheap-conflict-window'. What deeper analyses are possible now that the daily-ops routine doesn't normally have headroom for?

What PROP-115 captured correctly that we keep: the OBSERVATION that tinker has cost headroom. We are choosing to redirect that headroom toward deeper analysis, not toward savings.

What PROP-115 Recommendation B captured that's NOT in scope here: the Haiku/script pre-flight gate (structural model-split). That's an engineering project, not a quiet-period activity. Defer per PROP-115's own deferral reasoning — we may revisit when dome returns and tinker is genuinely cycle-constrained.

Other-side checks operator already considered:
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Spending more during quiet period is wasteful if we can save it.' Counter: quota is not constrained (38% weekly pace, well below ceiling). The marginal cost of an Opus tinker run is a fraction of a percent of weekly quota. Marginal value of deep-mode tinker work goes to ZERO once dome breaks drought (no time, no cycles). Now is the cheap-to-spend window.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Tinker daily routine ops are already adequate; deeper analysis just makes work.' Counter: tinker self-reported FND-1 MODERATE this run (PROP-115 itself) plus FND-2 MINOR (re-review detector still over-counts). The fact that tinker has cycles to author propose-only PROPs suggests it has bandwidth for more substantive analyses than its current routine demands.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Open-ended directives produce vague outputs.' Counter: this directive enumerates SPECIFIC candidate explorations below. Tinker picks the highest-value 1-3, rank-orders them, and reports back. Not a blank check.
task: Author a propose-only PROP (PROP-116 or amendment to PROP-115) that catalogs deeper-analysis modes tinker could spend cycles on during the quiet period. Rank by expected forward-value (specifically: 'what would save us more time/risk/cost AFTER dome breaks drought'). Recommend top 1-3 for operator selection. The operator will then commission specific deep-dives via subsequent directives.

candidate_explorations.A_prop_graph_archaeology: Walk all ~115 PROPs. Build a dependency graph (supersedes/superseded_by/amends/depends_on). Identify: which are still load-bearing, which are OBE-but-not-marked, which have wrongly-marked verification_pattern status, which dependency chains have broken links. PROP-102 auto-close is mechanical; this is the judgment layer above it. Output: a one-time PROP-graph audit report identifying ~10-20 candidates for cleanup before they pollute the auto-close trust graph.
candidate_explorations.B_prompt_cost_archaeology: PROP-112 step-cost-history now has ~7 days of decider + integrity per-step data. Identify the top-3 highest-cost step buckets across both agents. For each, examine the prompt section that fires that step — is it justified? Could it be slimmed (PROP-111 1B-style rare-path move to a reference module)? Author concrete diffs for the top 1-2 candidates, propose-only. Mirror PROP-111 1A/1C structure.
candidate_explorations.C_pre_active_period_readiness_audit: Walk the analyst→curmudgeon→decider chain mentally simulating dome-breaks-drought conditions (e.g., 3 new WINs in a day). Identify weak links: where would HOL blocking emerge, where would cost spike, where would integrity findings cascade. Pre-emptively author proposals for 1-2 highest-risk weak links. Goal: make the active-period transition smoother.
candidate_explorations.D_disaster_recovery_playbook_expansion: PROP-051 covers workspace-sync mass-delete disaster shape. Other shapes lack explicit playbooks: (a) chronic decider 403 cascade, (b) FUSE total unmount, (c) GitHub API outage, (d) PAT revoked mid-pipeline, (e) integrity false-negative on a real drift, (f) prune-integrity over-deletes despite the 2000 cap. Pick the 2 most-likely shapes and author propose-only playbooks (detect + diagnose + recover + verify).
candidate_explorations.E_documentation_hygiene_pass: Walk monitor/prompts/*.md identifying outdated sections that no longer match implementation. CLAUDE.md too. Common shapes: stale cadence numbers, outdated PROP references, agents promoted/demoted but doc not updated. Author a propose-only consolidated edit list — high signal-to-noise.
candidate_explorations.F_cost_projection_model: Build a forward-looking cost projection: if dome activity returns at intensity X (e.g., 2 new WINs/week, 5 new ISSs/week), what's our daily/weekly burn? Where are the bottlenecks? Operator uses this to decide whether to permanently ship PROP-115 Recommendation B (Haiku gate) or whether we have headroom.
candidate_explorations.G_hnote_consumption_audit: Trace a sample of historical operator HNOTEs through the consuming agent. Verify the action taken matches the intent. Tinker has the unique position to do this cross-agent — it sees all the artifacts. Goal: catch any HNOTE that was miscompiled.
candidate_explorations.H_archive_integrity_audit: PROP-022 archive files have been accumulating for weeks. Spot-check: any corruption, any silent truncation, any drift from the live counterparts? This is critical infrastructure that we don't actively monitor.
candidate_explorations.I_tinker_self_audit: Yesterday tinker noted its own context grew +15.4% since 2026-06-10 (PROP-102 + PROP-108 prose). Self-audit tinker.md + reference modules: which sections fire most/least often per Mode? Author own prompt-slim recommendation, propose-only.

deliverable: A propose-only PROP file (PROP-116 or PROP-115 amendment) containing: (1) brief evaluation of each candidate A-I above (in scope? doable in a single tinker run? forward-value high?); (2) rank-ordered top 3 by expected forward-value, with the value criterion explicit; (3) for the #1 recommendation, a one-paragraph scope statement the operator can convert to a subsequent commissioning directive; (4) honest assessment of which candidates tinker DOESN'T think are worth doing.
constraints: Propose-only. Tinker does NOT execute any deep audit in the same run that authors PROP-116. Operator selects from the proposed deep-dives and commissions specifically.
Honor the existing tinker schedule — don't propose changes to dome-tinker cron in this PROP. PROP-115 Rec A is explicitly REJECTED; further schedule discussion is out of scope.
Lean toward forward-value over breadth. Three well-scoped deep-dives are more useful than nine shallow ones.

If tinker thinks the operator's reframe is wrong, say so explicitly with reasoning. The operator wants tinker's judgment, not compliance theater. PROP-115's cost analysis was rigorous and operator's reframe is a strategic choice that doesn't refute the cost data — tinker is entitled to disagree about strategy too.
Don't relitigate PROP-115 Recommendation B (Haiku gate). It's deferred for separate consideration.

Once dome returns, tinker time becomes precious (competition for cycles).
Now (cheap) is the right time to do deep analysis whose forward-value lasts into the active period.
Quota is not constrained — ~38% weekly pace, well below ceiling.
Throttle decision can wait until we've harvested the deep-value work AND cost pressure emerges.
